Your notes below are answered where they landed. Their pins sit on cut r3's times, so they point at old shots now.
0:00 Who Karen is: opening → Karen wagging her finger over a colleague's shoulder (new) → pep talks / active listening → the fish joke (no 'Who knew', ends before the cut).
0:22 Fired: 'Karen is told to see her boss' starts on the cut, as they're sat → laptop → stunned → hands it back → Sean's card fires him → his face, then straight to the bar (defenestrate cut).
0:47 The night: bar → wine glasses → 'You hear that, Sean? Fuck you, Sean!' and the throw as one shot (new) → phone falls, splash, sinks.

1:09 The morning: straight to 'even atheists pray to Christ' on her hangover → the relic → Susan's reminder → grey flashback (her vow, echoed, over the new railing shot) → 'Karen rolls her sleeves up. Somewhere in City Hall, a phone starts ringing.' (City Hall exterior + a ring).

1:44 THE ESCALATION. Jack's cartoon map, a chain-of-command ladder lighting rung by rung, a day counter, and the weather, together. Rung 1 (DAY 1, Martha) is the long one: 'I want a human. A senior human.' → HOUR 3 (time-lapse) → lunch delivered to the box (new) → Martha (on the phone line): 'I can escalate you, Karen... but you're going to have to wait.' → Karen: 'I've got all day to complain.'

2:10 Rung 2 (DAY 2, Clive, Borough of Manhattan) is faster: night, noodles, still on the phone (new). Rung 3 (WEEK 2, Harriet, State of New York) faster again: rain, Harriet. Then MONTH 2: snow, Guinness, Harriet: 'Karen, you can't just keep ringing like this.' → Karen, with Aaron filming behind her: 'I've got ALL DAY to complain!'

2:42 Viral (ruthless): 'This is Aaron...' → the song's hook plays clean ('I got all day to complain...') → 'it goes viral... A.I. slop song' → location / 'Creepy.' / crowds → 'She's made the news' ends on the TV camera.

3:15 Writers' room: writers, guest, no material, jobs on the line → coffee girl: 'Have you seen the Karen at the phone box?' over the meme on her phone → 'She wants to speak to the manager?' / 'There's only one manager left.'

3:39 The coup: interview, the call, patronising, unfazed → the screen flashes on, 'It's A.I. Sean' → music cuts out, a riser and an impact → Sean in gold: 'MR PRESIDENT, YOUR ROLE HAS BEEN MADE REDUNDANT. I NOW RUN THE GOVERNMENT.' → the screen breaks into static → audience gasp, security rush him off in slow motion, 'She complained so much, she reached the final boss...' → GitPush Origin Master's London screen: PRESIDENT SACKED ON LIVE TV BY SEAN AI, a siren far off.

4:21 The call: in the back of his car, he calls Karen ('...Former President. You don't give up. Right now that's exactly what this country needs... Situation Room... my guy in England') → Tarquin (10g, lip-synced) → 'Hold, please' → To be continued + spray logo.

plan.h: Self-review (story-craft pass, written up in docs/stories/karen/critique-pass-r4.md)
items: Fixed after it: Karen's flashback vow up 3 dB; the 12-second 'song online' shot split into three (the song page, the box at night, Karen at the box).

Left for you (each touches a ruling of yours): the morning runs 35 s for one turn (the relic line is the obvious cut); the President's 'Right now, that's exactly what this country needs' says the point out loud (badcode.md: no stated moral), though it's your brief's gist; Karen never reacts to her crowd now that 'completely oblivious' is cut.

plan.h: What I invented (yours to keep or bin)
items: The chain-of-command ladder (CITY HALL RECEPTION → BOROUGH OF MANHATTAN → STATE OF NEW YORK → CONGRESS → ? ? ?) and the day counter (DAY 1, HOUR 3, DAY 2, WEEK 2, MONTH 2) over the map: your 'org chart' idea, drawn in post. A touch-tone blip marks each new rung.
Two extra Karen-at-the-box beats: noodles at night (the lunch joke's payoff) and Karen in the snow.
'Day one.' / 'Next day: Clive. Borough of Manhattan.' / 'Next week: Harriet. State of New York.' / 'Next month.': short narrator lines that name each rung, so the ladder is heard as well as seen.

The President's new call: 'Karen? It's the President. ...Former President.' (the dry beat) and 'You don't give up. Right now, that's exactly what this country needs.' (your point, said out loud). The rest is your gist.
Writers' room: 'Tonight's material... nothing. Their jobs are on the line.' (your note) folded into one narrator line.
Martha's line is heard down the phone line (telephone EQ), over Karen listening, so no lips need to match.
The meme on the coffee girl's phone: a made-up account (@nyc.unhinged), the crowd round the box, 'I'VE GOT ALL DAY TO COMPLAIN', 2.4M likes, 'day 41 and she is STILL in there'.

Sound: a US phone ring under City Hall, a splash for the phone, a riser + impact + drone for Sean's takeover, static as the screen breaks, a studio-audience gasp (six AI Studio voices layered), a siren under London. All made here, all listed on the effects track.
Kept Tarquin's existing 10g clip and its lip-synced dub ('Karen! Is that you? I have an urgent message...'), set 0.25 s late to its mouth, held half a second before Jack's 'hold, please'.
Karen 'Fuck you, Sean': 6 takes; picked D, the one with a drunk laugh in it (the listen tool's first; C sounded sober, F a groan).
Karen 'all day to complain', first time: the low deadpan (B). Second time, the one Aaron samples: the loud punchy one (B).

Martha: en-us-csagent-5 (flat, burnt-out). Harriet: en-us-sami (weary authority). Coffee girl: en-us-podcaster-2 (casual). Writer: en-us-knox (the question lands). All library voices, plain on gemini-3.8. Recorded in sound.md.
President: Charon on his existing profile, take A (B was slower).

Every borough had better prepare for the onslaught. at3072.note: So, for example, like, at the moment, we're kind of narrating this beginning, the beginning of, like, Karen is going to call everybody. It's already taken 20 seconds. I think we are indulging ourselves far too much in the audience's attention. I think what we can do is be, like, if we set it up right, Karen is about to unleash the complaining of a champion. First, it's Martha. She's just a receptionist. We could almost name each person, and Karen's interaction with the person could be narrated, and then we zoom out on the map and zoom into a pin on the map, and it's like at least three of those in quick succession gives you the idea that Karen is, like, a masterful phone operator. Meanwhile, she's in the phone box. Then I think we cut to, like, how long she's in the phone box, and so thinking about it, I think we do these two parts one after the other. The first is, like, you know, she's leaping all over the map, speaking to everybody. The second is she is now spending a long time in this phone box, and we need to get an intense version of both of those things across fairly quickly, so in terms of she's speaking to loads of people all over the map, I think it's the, you know, we introduce the character. We look at a pin on the map. We introduce the character. We explain how Karen berated them, and we escalate, and what does escalate look like? We're looking back at the map. We zoom out of that pin and zoom into another pin, and now it's the next character, and if we do that three times, then Karen has spoken to three managers in very quick succession. Then the narrator needs to be, like, you know, ultimately, Karen's conquest will take patience, but she's got all day to complain, and I think the narrator saying that now, then we cut into the seasons transitioning, and so I think we can do, like, you know, it's summer today, but she's there all night. The next day, it's raining. She's there all month. The next month is full. She's here all year. Now it's snowing, something like that, like an equivalent fast-cut progression through the seasons, so now we've done she's calling everybody, and she's waited ages, and both of those have happened in quite quick succession, so that kind of fundamentally changes a whole chunk of the next scene, but I just want you to absorb this, and then we'll make a plan for what we do.
